- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 2–5% if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- If sentiment shows strong negative bias (≥0.67) in last 3–5 days, model overcorrects downward; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is mixed or low (≤0.33) and recent price action is trending down; apply upward bias of 1–2% for 3–7 day horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion after strong trends; apply smoothing filter: if 5-day moving average of forecast > 70, reduce by 1–2% for next 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment momentum.
